properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-07, after a video on maintainers being unable to keep up with the volume of code AI generates, and seeing the same at work.

HIS WORDS: "One of the things the video promoted as a solution was typings and having contracts. That is in-line with the MOSA work already discussed many times. It is in line with coming up with Systems Engineering 'black boxes' where you have contracts/interfaces between different systems or components. Even in python 3.10's modern approach, you now have: def find(user_id: int) -> str | None:, which is in a way, a small contract for that function and also allows a reviewer to quickly see what the function does without reading the whole function body. This brainstorm is about how do we enforce contracts and typings for coding projects. For non-coding projects, maybe using accepted industry practices or having the agent use standards is appropriate. In a nutshell, this brainstorm is about 'enforcing' the agent to use typings, protocols, interface contracts, standards, 'building codes', etc that are appropriate for a given domain for the design project. This reduces the burden on reviewers/maintainers of a design while also increasing the 'trust-worthiness' or 'believeability' of a design produced using reflow2. In some ways, this is like making the /root-cause skill more automatic due to agents often being over-confident in identifying a fix to a problem. This is similar in that AI can quickly build a design and it can be a pile of garbage and hard to review and full of bugs. These are kind of 'checks' that reflow2 is trying to enforce upon the agent to be more rigorous and deliver designs (and code in coding projects) that is easy to review."

TWO MEASUREMENTS TAKEN WHILE RECORDING THIS, because both change which options are open.

(1) THE NON-CODING HALF IS ALREADY IN THE SCHEMA AND HAS NEVER BEEN USED. `EnvironmentRule` declares exactly this vocabulary, and its `rule_type` enum reads: regulatory, building_code, zoning, safety, environmental, standard, physical_law, interface, constraint. His phrase "building codes" is a value in a schema written months ago. ZERO EnvironmentRule nodes exist in this graph, no tool constructs one, and `decision:vocab:environment` PARKED the whole domain as deliberately unused UNTIL A USER ASKS FOR IT. This is a user asking for it.

(2) A CONTRACT CAN NOW CARRY EVIDENCE, AND A RECORDED FACT SAYS OTHERWISE. `fact:a-contract-is-the-one-thing-reflow2-cannot-attach-evidence-to` (2026-08-21) states that VERIFIES cannot target an Interface, "and interfaces are the nodes MOSA turns on". Measured today: VERIFIES now legally targets Artifact, Capability, Component, Constraint, DesignRule, Interface and Requirement. That fact is STALE and should be invalidated, and its staleness matters here because it would tell the next reader that the most promising option below is impossible.

OPTIONS, UNRANKED, each with what is cheap or expensive about it:

(a) DECLARE THE REGIME AND CHECK NOTHING. The design states which contract vocabulary applies — Python typing, OpenAPI, MIL-STD-1553, the IBC — and reflow2 reports its absence. Cheap. And it repeats the exact failure this project measured twice today: `Verification.level` exists and nothing reads it, so a second unread property would make the design SAY more and KNOW no more.

(b) BUILD THE ENVIRONMENT COMPLIANCE LAYER THAT IS ALREADY DESIGNED. `dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built` is open and is precisely the non-coding half: a rule the design must comply with, with COMPLIES_WITH and VIOLATES edges to reach it. The vocabulary costs nothing because it exists; what it needs is a constructor (EnvironmentRule is one of three types with no typed write tool at all) and something that READS the edges. Against it: it was parked for a reason, and building a compliance layer nobody has yet used on a real design risks the same unread-property fate.

(c) A BLACK BOX OWES A CONTRACT, THE WAY A CAPABILITY OWES A REQUIREMENT. Already open as `dec:idea-a-black-box-owes-an-interface-the-way-a-capability-owes-a-requirement`. This is the structural floor beneath everything else: you cannot claim a component without stating its boundary. Cheap, computable today, and it says nothing about whether the contract is any GOOD.

(d) CARRY THE EXTERNAL CHECKER'S RESULT AS EVIDENCE, AND DO NOT REIMPLEMENT IT. For code the checker already exists — mypy, pyright, cargo, a schema validator — and reflow2's job is to be the place its result LANDS and STAYS ATTACHED, not to become a type checker. A Verification against the Interface, with a real last_run_at. Newly possible per measurement (2). It generalises to the non-coding case without stretching: a structural engineer's stamp, a lab certificate and a test report are all somebody else's check whose result the design must carry. It also fits `req:the-agent-never-authors-what-requires-accountable-sign-off`, which already says the agent carries the requirement into the tool and the result back as evidence. Against it: it proves a check RAN, never that the contract is honest.

(e) MAKE REVIEWABILITY ITSELF THE REPORTED NUMBER — what fraction of components state a boundary, what fraction of published contracts carry a passing check, how much of the design a reviewer would have to read to trust it. Answers his actual complaint rather than a proxy for it. Expensive to define honestly, and easy to turn into a score that gets gamed.

(f) DO NOTHING. Typing is the language's job and standards are the user's.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO ALL OF IT, and it bounds every option above: REFLOW2 CANNOT READ THE CODE. It can require that a contract be stated, that a check exist, and that the check have run and passed — it cannot verify that a function signature tells the truth about the body beneath it. Claiming otherwise would be the renderer-fill-in failure at the scale of a whole discipline. What reflow2 can honestly offer is the SECOND leg: not the check, but the demand for one and the record of its result.

AND HIS OWN ANALOGY IS THE SHARPEST THING HERE. He compares this to making /root-cause automatic, and that comparison was tested today: the mechanism that worked was not a rule, a nudge or a reminder — it was a TOOL DESCRIPTION THAT DEMANDS THE SKILL AT THE MOMENT OF THE WRITE, because a tool description is the one thing an agent reliably reads while working. If contracts are to be enforced on an agent rather than requested of it, that is the shape with evidence behind it, and it is a different shape from any of (a) to (f).
properties.name: OPEN — how does reflow2 make an agent USE the typings, protocols, contracts and standards a domain already has, so a design stays reviewable at the speed AI produces it?
properties.rationale:
Recorded rather than acted on because the question spans a settled schema layer nobody has used, two already-open decisions, and a claim about what reflow2 may honestly assert — and because the option that looks strongest, carrying somebody else's checker result as evidence, only became possible when VERIFIES gained Interface as a target, which no record currently reflects.

The motivation is worth keeping separate from the mechanism: he is not asking for more vocabulary, he is asking that a design produced fast stay REVIEWABLE and BELIEVABLE. Any option that adds a property nobody reads makes the design longer and no more trustworthy, which is the specific failure to test each of these against.
